mission.title: Install and Configure Vultr Kubernetes Engine (VKE)
mission.description: This mission guides you through installing the Vultr Kubernetes Engine (VKE), a managed Kubernetes service that simplifies cluster management on Vultr's infrastructure. It is ideal for users looking for a fully managed solution with integrated cloud features, but it may have limitations in customization compared to self-managed clusters.

steps.title: Install the Vultr CLI
steps.description:
This step installs the Vultr CLI, which is necessary for managing your Vultr resources.

```bash

curl -LO https://github.com/vultr/vultr-cli/releases/download/v1.0.0/vultr-cli_linux_amd64.tar.gz

tar -xzf vultr-cli_linux_amd64.tar.gz

sudo mv vultr-cli /usr/local/bin/

vultr-cli version

```

> Download the latest CLI version.
> Extract the downloaded tarball.
> Move the CLI binary to your PATH.
> Verify the installation.

steps.title: Create a Kubernetes Cluster
steps.description:
This step creates a new Kubernetes cluster on Vultr with the specified version and node count.

```bash

vultr-cli k8s create --name my-cluster --region lon1 --version 1.30 --node-count 3

```

> Replace 'my-cluster' with your desired cluster name.

steps.title: Set Up Kubeconfig
steps.description:
This step configures your kubeconfig file to connect to the newly created cluster.

```bash

vultr-cli k8s kubeconfig my-cluster > ~/.kube/config

```

> This command saves the kubeconfig to the default location.

steps.title: Verify Cluster Nodes
steps.description:
This step checks the status of the nodes in your cluster to ensure they are running.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> You should see all nodes in 'Ready' status.

steps.title: Post-Install Configuration
steps.description:
This step sets up autoscaling and monitoring for your cluster.

```bash

kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/master/cluster-autoscaler/cloudprovider/vultr/examples/cluster-autoscaler.yaml

kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/monitoring/master/monitoring.yaml

```

> This command deploys the cluster autoscaler.
> This command deploys monitoring tools.

uninstall.title: Delete the Kubernetes Cluster
uninstall.description:
This step removes the Kubernetes cluster and all associated resources. Be aware that this will lead to data loss.

```bash

vultr-cli k8s delete my-cluster

```

> Replace 'my-cluster' with your cluster name.

upgrade.title: Upgrade the Kubernetes Cluster
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you back up your data. This step performs the upgrade and verifies the cluster status.

```bash

kubectl get nodes -o wide

vultr-cli k8s upgrade my-cluster --version 1.31

kubectl get nodes

```

> Check the current node status before upgrading.
> Replace 'my-cluster' with your cluster name.
> Verify that all nodes are in 'Ready' status after the upgrade.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Failed to connect to the server'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This may occur if the kubeconfig is not set up correctly or the cluster is down.

**Fix:**
Ensure your kubeconfig is correctly configured and the cluster is running.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Insufficient resources available'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the requested resources exceed the available capacity in your Vultr account.

**Fix:**
Check your Vultr account for resource limits and adjust your cluster size accordingly.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Node not ready'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This may happen if the node is still initializing or has failed to join the cluster.

**Fix:**
Check the node status and logs for any errors using 'kubectl describe node <node-name>'.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'LoadBalancer service pending'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the LoadBalancer is not being provisioned correctly by the Vultr Cloud Controller Manager.

**Fix:**
Ensure that the Vultr Cloud Controller Manager is correctly deployed and configured.

versionNotes.changes: Added support for automatic LoadBalancer provisioning and improved node resource management.
versionNotes.migrationSteps: No specific migration steps required for this version.

resolution.summary: You should see a list of nodes with 'Ready' status when running 'kubectl get nodes'.

prerequisites.description: Ensure you have the Vultr CLI and kubectl installed and configured.
